To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the water-soluble host-guest-type catalysts derived from calixarenes were successfully designed, synthesized, and characterized.
water-soluble acid catalysts derived from calix[6]-arene were synthesized, and the catalytic activity of the catalysts was investigated.
water-soluble host molecules derived from calixarenes were found to catalyze a hydration reaction of a substrate according to Michaelis–Menten kinetics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel class of acid catalysts based on calix[6]-arene, which is a new class of acid catalyst.
the synthesis and properties of calixarenes, especially water-soluble ones.
the design and synthesis of new host molecules and their applications to the development of new functional materials and molecular devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
calixarene-based host molecules can be used for the design of new functionalized host molecules with potential applications as catalysts.
the host-guest-type acid catalysts derived from calix[6]-arenes can be applied to various organic reactions in water.
calixarene-based host molecules can be used as a new type of host-guest-type acid catalysts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calixarene-based host-guest catalysts are useful in the design of artificial enzymes.
we have developed new water-soluble acid catalytic systems based on calixarene, and have found that these systems have a high catalytic activity in water.
calixarene is an ideal host molecule to be used as a host-guest type catalyst.

the calixarene framework is a useful platform to design host-guest type acid catalysts.
calixarene derivatives can be used as a host-guest-type catalyst.
calixarene-based host molecules can be used as catalysts for the hydration reaction.
